cards.explanation: The answer is flint, friends. The LORD tells Joshua, “Make flint knives and circumcise the sons of Israel once again.” Then Joshua makes them (Joshua 5:2-3). I'm a cookie stamper, so my whole toolbox is one handle with my name carved in it. Knife making is way above my pay grade.

The answer is that none of them had been circumcised. Not one. The text says it plainly: “…none of those born in the wilderness on the journey from Egypt had been circumcised.” The ones who came out of Egypt were circumcised, but their sons born along the way were not (Joshua 5:5). That's a whole generation waiting on Joshua's flint knives.

The answer is that they did not obey the LORD. That's the reason the text gives: “…since they did not obey the LORD.” So the LORD vowed never to let them see the land He had sworn to their fathers (Joshua 5:6). The wandering went on until those men of war had died. No guessing needed here, friends, because the verse tells us why.

The answer is False. Joshua 5:6 says the LORD “…vowed never to let them see the land He had sworn to their fathers to give us…” It's the land flowing with milk and honey, and that generation of men of war died without seeing it. I think that's a heavy one, so I'll just say it once and let it sit.

The answer is healed. Joshua 5:8 says that after the whole nation had been circumcised, they stayed there in the camp until they were healed. They stayed put. I know a little about staying put, since I once spent years in the back of a junk drawer. Nobody was healing me back there, I was just collecting dust.

The answer is Gilgal, friends. The LORD says, “Today I have rolled away the reproach of Egypt from you.” Then the verse tells us, “So that place has been called Gilgal to this day.” (Joshua 5:9). That "…to this day." means the name was still in use when the writer wrote it. It's the same camp the Israelites are in when they keep the Passover (Joshua 5:10).

The answer is the Passover. Joshua 5:10 says that on the evening of the fourteenth day of the month, while camped at Gilgal on the plains of Jericho, the Israelites kept it. Before that, the LORD had said, “Today I have rolled away the reproach of Egypt from you.” (Joshua 5:9). Keep that evening in mind, friends.

The answer is unleavened bread and roasted grain, and it all came from the produce of the land. Joshua 5:11 says they ate it the day after the Passover, on that very day. I'm a cookie guy, so I went looking for chocolate chips in that verse and came up empty. Bread and roasted grain from the land is what the text gives.

The answer is the manna. Joshua 5:12 says, “…the manna ceased. There was no more manna for the Israelites…” That year they began to eat the crops of the land of Canaan. Nobody said anything about missing it, so I'll just say the cookies in my bakery never come with a stop date.
